🌙 The Much-Awaited School Sleepover Is Here!

 

Dear Parents and Learners,

 

The excitement is building! One of the most awaited experiences of the year is just around the corner – *our School Sleepover!* 🎉

 

Get ready for an evening filled with fun, laughter, friendship and special memories as our learners enjoy staying back at school, spending time with their friends and experiencing the joy of a night away from home in a familiar school environment.

 

To help everyone prepare for this exciting experience, please refer to the packing checklist below.

 

🧳 Sleepover Packing Checklist

 

1. Rucksack / small suitcase - 1 (measurement - 115cm)
2. Dress - 2 sets
3. Sweatshirt / Jacket - 1
4. Night dress full sleeves & full length - 1
5. Towel and hand towel - 1 each
6. Personal hygiene kit (toothbrush, paste, face wash, comb, etc)
7. Bedsheet - 1
8. Blanket/Quilt - 1
9. Pillow - 1
10. Floaters in foot wear
11. Board games / UNO cards (if required)

 

A Few Important Reminders

 

- Please pack all belongings in a **small, portable suitcase** so that learners can independently manage and organise their own belongings.
- Kindly label all personal belongings with your child's name to avoid mix-ups.
- Parents of learners who usually travel by school bus but wish to pick up their child directly from the school premises on Saturday, 14 November 2026, at 8:00 a.m. are requested to email the school by Friday, 13 November 2026, before 3:00 p.m.

 

Let's get those bags packed and the excitement rolling!

 

Here's to a night of giggles, friendship, adventure and memories that will last a lifetime! 🌟

 

Thank you for your cooperation and support.

As discussed, please find below the details for your weekend project work, "Research and Make a Fossil."

1. Research a Fossil

Choose one fossil and find out:

This week's reading is the book Counting on Katherine: How Katherine Johnson saved Apollo 13

You've likely heard of the historic Apollo 13 moon landing. But do you know about the mathematical genius who made sure that Apollo 13 returned safely home? As a child, Katherine Johnson loved to count. She counted the steps on the road, the number of dishes and spoons she washed in the kitchen sink, everything! Boundless, curious, and excited by calculations, young Katherine longed to know as much as she could about math, about the universe. From Katherine's early beginnings as a gifted student to her heroic accomplishments as a prominent mathematician at NASA, this is the story of a groundbreaking American woman who not only calculated the course of moon landings but, in turn, saved lives and made enormous contributions to history.

 

Happy Reading!

Dear Learners,

Here are some ideas to help you work on your project topics house-wise. You can use these ideas as a starting point and add your own creative ideas to make your project more interesting, informative, and unique.

Remember, these are just suggestions—feel free to think creatively and add your own ideas to make your topic the best!

 

Aquila – Unsung Heroes: Who Gets Recognised and Who Doesn’t?

Idea: “Heroes We Know & Heroes We Don’t” poster. One side famous people, other side everyday heroes (cleaner, farmer, nurse, parent).
Impact tip: Interview one school staff member and add their photo or quote.

Draco – Needs, Money and Community: Who Helps When Money Is Not Enough?

Idea: Chart showing Needs → What money can buy → Who helps when money is not enough (family, school, community, government).
Impact tip: Give one real local example (mid-day meal, free books, hospital, etc.).

Leo – Built to Survive: Amazing Adaptations

Idea: “Animal Adaptation Cards” – Make 4–5 cards. Each card has a picture of an animal + one adaptation + why it helps.
Impact tip: Choose animals from different biomes (camel, polar bear, cactus, penguin) so it looks varied and colourful.

Tarus – The Journey of a Product: How the World Is Connected

Idea: “Journey of a Chocolate / Mobile Phone / T-shirt” flowchart. Show the steps from raw material → factory → shop → home with simple pictures and arrows.
Impact tip: Highlight 2–3 countries involved so students see global connection clearly.

 

Be creative, work together as a team, and make your project something you are proud to share

Dear Parents,

Greetings!

The Primary Humanitas Fest – HUMANVERSE 2026, held today, was a wonderful celebration of learning, creativity and collaboration across Grades 2–5. We are delighted to share that our learners put up an excellent showcase of their Humanities learning through their creative displays, models and presentations.

It was truly inspiring to witness our young learners take ownership of their learning and demonstrate student agency at every step. Their enthusiasm and confidence were evident as they shared their ideas, made decisions, explored different possibilities and worked together as a team. It was heartwarming to see how they listened to one another, built on each other's ideas, divided responsibilities and transformed their thoughts into meaningful projects.

Beyond the displays and presentations, what stood out was the learners' ability to think independently, collaborate purposefully, communicate their understanding and take pride in their work. Every effort reflected their curiosity, creativity, commitment and the joy of learning.

We would like to extend our heartfelt gratitude to all our parents for your encouragement, cooperation and support throughout the preparation for HUMANVERSE. Your involvement, motivation and willingness to support your children played a significant role in making this event a memorable experience. Thank you for giving our learners the confidence and encouragement to explore, create and express themselves.

The results of HUMANVERSE 2026 will be announced on 12 November 2026. We look forward to sharing the results with you!

As we celebrate the success of this event, we hope our learners carry forward the confidence, curiosity, teamwork and enthusiasm they demonstrated today into all their future learning experiences.

Thank you once again for being such an important part of our learning community and for helping us make HUMANVERSE 2026 a meaningful celebration of learning!

Warm regards,
Primary Humanities Team
